sentences.text: 1 in question, she has falsely implicated him in the crime in question.
It is further argued that there is considerable delay in lodging the F.I.R.
It is further argued that the appellant was confined in the house of the victim female child till the matter was not reported to the police and, as such, this is case of false implication.

It is further argued that in the medical examination conducted by PW-5,
Dr. Malvika Kumud, no evidence of commission of rape was found.
(3.) The learned APP opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
(4.) We have considered the submission so advanced.
We have also considered the record on proceedings including evidence of the victim female child, the investigator as well as the medical officer.
(5.) This is a case relating to commission of penetrative sexual assault on a female child who was reportedly 15 years of age at the time of the incidence.
Evidence on record indicates that father of the victim female child had died long back.
Her mother was deaf and dumb.
Some of the villagers including PW-3 Samsul Khatoon was taking care of this destitute family.
(6.) On this background it is an evidence of the victim Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.874 of 2022(7) dt.18-05-2023 female child/PW-2

that on 17.12.2020, when there was nobody in her house,
the appellant entered in her house and forcibly committed rape on her.

She further deposed that then villagers gathered and confined the appellant in one room of her house but subsequently,
Mukhiya of the village alongwith few others came and forcibly took away the appellant with them.
Thereafter, the victim female child lodged the report which has resulted in registration of the crime in question.

(7.) The capital is sought to be made out of the statement figuring in paragraph no. 6 of the cross-examination of the victim female child to the effect that no panchayati at the village was held and villagers have not been insisted the appellant to marry the victim female child.

Similarly,
support is sought to be drawn from statement of the investigator in paragraph no. 11 of this cross-examination to the effect that the villagers took meeting of the panchayat and as the appellant refused to marry, subsequently the F.I.R. came to be lodged.

(8.) It is not the defence of the appellant that he was having any love relations with the victim female child or that the victim female child was insisting in to marry her and as he refused to marry her, the victim female child has falsely implicated him in a false case.

When such is not the defence, Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.874 of 2022(7) dt.18-05-2023 stray sentences in cross-examination of the investigator or the victim female child cannot be construed to mean that the appellant is falsely implicated in the crime in question as he refused to marry the victim female child.
(9.) The delay in lodging the F.I.R. cannot be a ritualistic formula to jettison the prosecution case.
In the case in hand there is implicit explanation to some delay in lodging the F.I.R.
There was no male member in the family of the victim female child.
Her father died since long back.
Her mother was deaf and dumb.
She was also not present in the house when the incident took place.

The appellant was apprehended on the spot and was confined in the house of the victim female child by the Mojabir Ansari vs The State Of Bihar on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108766268/
2 villagers but subsequently he was forcibly freed by Mukhiya of the village and few of his associates.

All these factors explain the delay in lodging the F.I.R.
(10.) When testimony of the victim of the sexual offence is clear, cogent and trustworthy then, there is no necessity of the same being corroborated by medical evidence.

Valuable reference to this proposition can be had from the judgement of the Supreme Court in the matter of B.C.Deva v. State of Karnataka reported in (2007) 12 SCC 122.
